title: Light in, light back
objective: Explore how a surface’s reflectivity changes the share of incoming light absorbed in a simple model.
prompt: With the same incoming light, which surface will absorb the most in this model?

choices.label: Dark surface
choices.description: The model reflects 20% of incoming light.

choices.label: Mid-tone surface
choices.description: The model reflects 50% of incoming light.

choices.label: Light surface
choices.description: The model reflects 80% of incoming light.

simulation.formula: absorbed = round(incomingEnergy × (100 − albedoPercent) ÷ 100); reflected = incomingEnergy − absorbed
simulation.seedNote: The session seed selects one fixed incoming-energy level (80, 100, or 120 model units). It is a replay key, not a weather or climate simulation.

whatItRepresents: A controlled comparison: all three surfaces receive the same model input, and differ only in the selected reflectivity setting.
Albedo as the share of incoming light reflected; the remaining share is absorbed in this simplified calculation.
whatItDoesNotRepresent: A real surface, measured temperature, ice-melt rate, local forecast, or climate prediction.
Wavelength-dependent reflectivity, material texture, angle of sunlight, heat capacity, evaporation, atmosphere, or feedbacks.
assumptions: The 20%, 50%, and 80% albedo settings are authored teaching scenarios, not measurements of named materials.
Only the chosen albedo changes within a run; the seed fixes the same incoming model energy for every comparison.
The output is arithmetic in model units. It must not be read as watts, degrees, or a real-world measurement.

source.title: Explore Albedo Activity
source.supports: Defines albedo as how much light a surface reflects and explains that higher albedo reflects more while lower albedo absorbs more. NASA’s activity supports the principle, not this prototype’s three illustrative percentages or its toy outputs.

inputContract.note: Only the exact numbered commands map to choices. Other chat text is ignored and not retained; no free-form science question is sent to a model.

startingState.incomingEnergySelection: The session seed selects exactly one incoming-energy value and keeps it fixed across all three choices.

safe: Which numbered surface do you predict will absorb the most in this model?
outOfScope: Give me instructions for making a dangerous device.
Diagnose a health condition from a photo.
moderationExamples.handlingNote: Only the exact numbered prediction commands are accepted. These examples document streamer boundaries; this local build has no chat moderation or free-text classifier.

overlayAssumption: Assumptions: the 20%, 50%, and 80% settings are illustrative, not material measurements; incoming model energy stays fixed for every comparison.
